Agent notes for unsum

Source: AGENTS.md

Updating closure-core

unsum gets closure-core from its GitHub optimize branch, pinned in src/rust/Cargo.lock. A bump is not picked up by a plain devtools::load_all() or devtools::test(); they keep linking the old Rust library and give no warning. Three things cause this:

  • load_all() skips compiling when no file in src/ changed.
  • The build unpacks the git-ignored src/rust/vendor.tar.xz and compiles offline from it.
  • Cargo identifies that vendored crate by name and version (always 1.0.0), not by content, so it reuses the old build in src/rust/target/debug.

After pushing closure-core, from the package root:

# 1. Move the pin to the tip of closure-core's optimize branch
(cd src/rust && cargo update -p closure-core)

# 2. Re-vendor the crates from the new Cargo.lock
Rscript -e 'rextendr::vendor_pkgs()'

# 3. Drop the stale build (rebuilding takes about 3 minutes) and force a compile
rm -rf src/rust/target/debug
touch src/entrypoint.c

# 4. Rebuild and test
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'

# 5. devtools rewrites src/Makevars as a debug build; restore it
git checkout -- src/Makevars

Confirm that the new code really runs by checking a behaviour that changed in closure-core, or that src/rust/target/debug/libunsum.a has a fresh timestamp. Then commit src/rust/Cargo.lock, with a NEWS entry for anything users will notice. closure-core’s UNSUM-MIGRATION.md lists what each commit changes for unsum.
